messages:
randall: quick question from yesterday's regression: when we remap guest PFNs during async offload, do we ever expose a short-lived alias where a kvcache reader can observe the old physical mapping? iirc we do a two-step: write new pfn, then clear old mapping. failing test suggests a window. anyone familiar with the exact sequence?

elen: yes, code path is in vmap_remap(). we currently do: atomically install new pfn (so new readers hit it), queue mmu notifier unmap for old pfn, then clear old mapping slot. That ordering was to reduce stalls on remap writes.

sam: we've seen flakes w/ guest page-faults where kvcache read returned stale pfn and caused a wrong DMA to be issued. logs show kvcache::read got a pointer into old backing just after remap.

miguel: sounds like a classic read-after-write visibility problem across CPU and MMU notifier ordering. Two axes: slow the writer (make remap wait for mmu notifier ack) or make reader robust (version/epoch check).

anya: preference is reader robustness. Writers are on critical eviction paths and we can't add 1ms waits. If we add a mapping_epoch on page metadata and bump it on any remap/unbind, readers can compare their seen epoch and fallback to slowpath if mismatch. slowpath does a retry/refetch and optionally block for notifier quiesce.

randall: sketch of epoch approach:
```
write path:
  page->mapping_epoch++;
  write_new_pfn(); // publish
  smp_wmb();
  page->mapping_epoch++;

read path:
  pre = page->mapping_epoch;
  smp_rmb();
  pfn = read_pfn();
  smp_rmb();
  post = page->mapping_epoch;
  if (pre != post) goto slowpath;
```
This gives a 2-slot epoch so readers can detect concurrent remap.

elen: that looks reasonable. cost-wise reading two atomics + comparisons is tiny for hot paths. slowpath frequency is the concern. We need telemetry for epoch-retry rate.

miguel: slowpath options:
- immediate retry loop (spin for short window) -> low latency if remap was tiny
- synchronous wait for mmu notifier ack -> guarantees safety but stalls reader
- fallback to host-copy/serialize path -> safe but expensive
I like: spin for up to X microseconds then escalate to notifier wait.

sam: for tests, add a deterministic fault injector that delays notifier callbacks and a microbench harness that simulates remap storms. We can measure retry rate and estimate cost per-op.

anya: agree. let's also add a per-page counter: epoch_retries and a global histogram so ops can alert if > threshold. This helps detect prod regressions.

offload-bot: CI: run/host-remap-smoke on gpu-64g-8 flaked 2/50 runs. Category: mmu-notifier-delay. https://ci.redwood.internal/abcs

randall: ok plan: (1) implement 2-slot epoch with smp barriers and fastpath checks (sam will prototype), (2) implement slowpath spin+escalate on mismatch (miguel will prototype), (3) add CI fault injection and telemetry counters (anya), (4) perf microbench to ensure reader overhead < 100ns on avg (elen). If results look good we avoid adding waits on writers.

miguel: one more consideration: multi-migration ordering across shared pages (coherency when two writers remap same page). epoch bumps should be monotonic and rely on atomic increment; readers need to tolerate wrap (use 64-bit epoch).

sam: I'll open a draft PR DRAFT: kvcache-epoch-fastpath with tests and CI knobs. Will include a flag to enable notifier-delay injection.

anya: don't forget to wire telemetry to observability (per-tenant counters) so SRE can alert on sustained retry spikes.

randall: perfect. posting this as follow-up note for the mem-mgmt RFC. thanks all. :raised_hands:
